subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog and recovery policy, and which actions are allowed by default versus explicit opt-in?
rationale: The requested behavior changes service restart, automatic repair, degraded startup, health disclosure, and operator notification semantics; source inspection cannot safely choose those security and product boundaries.

options.title: Keep Design Umbrella
options.body: Use this issue to hold the maintainer-approved core policy, then land narrower PRs for crash-loop breaker, watchdog probe, recovery actions, health schema, and notification behavior.

options.title: Delegate To Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close this only after every remaining slice is explicitly moved to open canonical issues such as the crash-recovery ladder and rescue-watchdog PR with this context linked there.

options.title: Reject Core Recovery Ownership
options.body: Document external supervisor or plugin-managed recovery as the supported path and avoid adding core automatic repair semantics for now.

recommendation.title: Keep Design Umbrella
recommendation.body: Use this issue to hold the maintainer-approved core policy, then land narrower PRs for crash-loop breaker, watchdog probe, recovery actions, health schema, and notification behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history on gateway health/runtime hardening and is the best available routing candidate for the product/security boundary choice.
